steps.title: An alarm rings from sleep
steps.done_when: an alarm set in the clock app rings on time while the phone sleeps under its shell's suspend
steps.guide: The shell or clock must set an RTC wake alarm before suspend (kernel-sysfs-power-wakelock). Not known yet which phone shells do; never tried in our labs.

steps.title: A day on one charge
steps.done_when: a day of mixed use - standby, calls, screen time - ends with charge left
steps.guide: Never measured. UBports keeps it as an endurance test (ubports-device-data).

steps.title: The codec attaches and stays
steps.done_when: the codec enumerates on its buses (SoundWire, I2S, I2C) and stays attached across the boot
steps.guide: surya WCD937x: a wrong aoncc address hung the boot (wcd937x-dt-aoncc); the sleep pin state drove reset low (microphone-codec-drops-off); the LPI mux from the vendor tree (2026-11-11-lpi-mux-from-vendor). Hazard: reading the LPASS pinctrl in debugfs hangs the phone.

steps.title: The screen follows rotation
steps.done_when: turning the phone turns the shell's screen
steps.guide: Never tried in our labs.

steps.title: The banner on the console
steps.done_when: /init's banner with a heartbeat reaches the host on the console, read as the lab user
steps.guide: The gadget serial must be the one the host's udev rule names, or the tty is root's (walleye-banner-serial-fix, walleye-try-banner2).

steps.title: The battery gauge reads true
steps.done_when: capacity, voltage and current read in power_supply agree with a meter within 5 % over a discharge
steps.guide: Test to write. surya read gauge averages in its standby run (2026-11-17-r3-partial-and-the-reset-after); walleye open (walleye-fuel-gauge). PMI8998-class gauges are still RFCs (pmi8998-fg-rfc).

steps.title: Our boot image packs as the device wants
steps.done_when: header version, offsets, page size, dtb placement and os word match the control where they should
steps.guide: Pack from the device's [boot] declaration and count it against the control (walleye walleye-bootimage). The helper packs header v0 only.

steps.title: Bootloader unlocked
steps.done_when: fastboot getvar all says unlocked: yes
steps.guide: Unlocking wipes the user's data and is the owner's act. Read the state before anything else (walleye google-walleye-bootloader-first-look, surya first-fastboot-probe).

steps.title: Brightness follows the light
steps.done_when: covering the light sensor dims the panel under auto-brightness
steps.guide: Never tried in our labs.

steps.title: The Bluetooth controller is up
steps.done_when: the controller is listed and powers on
steps.guide: surya done; walleye open (walleye-wifi-wcn3990).

steps.title: Bluetooth pairs and carries sound
steps.done_when: a headset pairs, plays and records, in a call too
steps.guide: surya open (bt-pairing).

steps.title: The keys report one event a press
steps.done_when: power and volume keys give one press and one release each, no chatter
steps.guide: surya: the volume-down key on the PMIC chatters (2026-11-18-screen-off-while-typing-key-events, surya-key-chatter-resin).

steps.title: The call's sound path exists
steps.done_when: the voice DSP path (q6voice on Qualcomm), its routing and a Voice Call UCM verb are present
steps.guide: surya: a TX topology sent silence; the uplink needs a 1-channel capture on TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3 (call-audio-on-surya, calls-q6voice-kernel, calls-voice-ucm-uplink). World gap: q6voice lives out of tree in diverging copies and nothing exists for AudioReach SoCs (ixit-sdm845-upstreaming-0).

steps.title: A call or a message wakes it
steps.done_when: a call rings and an SMS arrives within 10 s while the phone sleeps
steps.guide: The IPCRTR glink wakeup plus ModemManager's quick suspend; reported not dependable on OnePlus 6 and Pixel 3a (qcom-wake-for-calls). World gap: waking for a call but not for chatter. surya open (sleep-wakes-for-calls).

steps.title: The camera bus binds
steps.done_when: the camera receiver (CAMSS: CSIPHY, CSID, VFE) and the control bus (CCI) bind
steps.guide: surya: CAMSS binds, no sensor described yet (2026-11-11-cameras-understood, surya-lab research/cameras.md).

steps.title: A viewable stream
steps.done_when: libcamera lists each camera and its ISP (software or hardware) gives a viewable stream
steps.guide: Today a software ISP, on the GPU since libcamera 0.7 (libcamera-softisp-fosdem-2026). World gap: the hardware ISP is not used on any Qualcomm phone (camss-stats-uapi-rfc).

steps.title: A charger power-on starts the charging screen, not the system
steps.done_when: plugged in while off, the phone starts a small charger mode that shows the level and turns the screen off again; the power key starts the full system
steps.guide: Android: the bootloader reads the power-on reason and passes androidboot.mode=charger; init then runs only the charger - the same kernel, no separate processor (Sailfish's act-dead mode, sailfish-hadk-checklist). World gap: no maintained charger mode in any mainline distribution; charging-sdl is unmaintained and boot-loops at low battery (pmaports-charging-sdl-1064).

steps.title: The charger online
steps.done_when: a power_supply of type USB appears, online follows the cable, and the voltage rises while connected
steps.guide: Until it works, tries are rationed by the battery. walleye c2: the charger defers on its tps61099 supplier (walleye-charger-wait-tps61099, walleye-charger-supplier).

steps.title: A complete phone
steps.done_when: every step it needs is done or not-needed
steps.guide: A goal: it does nothing itself - done when every hard need is done or not-needed, read off tad q bringup-chain (its ready is its done). A group of groups, as a systemd target is (systemd-target). Everything the hardware does, lasting: VoLTE, MMS, every radio and sensor, video, rollback, reliability. Apps and services (Android apps, banking, sync, backup) stay features, not steps.

steps.title: A known-good image boots from memory
steps.done_when: fastboot boot of a known-good stock-format image leaves fastboot and runs, nothing written
steps.guide: The control tells 'the bootloader refuses' from 'our image is wrong' (walleye walleye-loaderror-control).

steps.title: A coprocessor crash is survived
steps.done_when: a coprocessor crashed on purpose restarts and its users - sound, modem, sensors - come back with no reboot
steps.guide: surya failing for audio after a DSP restart (surya-adsp-audio-after-suspend-loop). World gap: nobody tests whole-stack recovery.

steps.title: A window on a dead boot
steps.done_when: a dead or hung boot leaves something the host reads: UART, pstore at the phone's own ramoops region, or a timing channel
steps.guide: On walleye ramoops survives only at the region the stock fdt names and only across a warm reset (walleye-pstore-warm-reset, walleye-pstore-t1-try); a timing channel told alive from dead (walleye-ml4-timing-channel); UART waits a cable (walleye-get-uart-setup).

steps.title: Repeated cycles stay clean
steps.done_when: 100 suspend cycles, 20 calls and 50 camera switches with no part lost
steps.guide: 'Does audio still work after two hours asleep' (weiss-fosdem-2025-missing-20).

steps.title: A daily-usable phone
steps.done_when: every step it needs is done or not-needed
steps.guide: A goal: it does nothing itself - done when every hard need is done or not-needed, read off tad q bringup-chain (its ready is its done). A group of groups, as a systemd target is (systemd-target). What a person needs every day: calls, messages, data, sound, a photo, a position, a day of battery, charging, updates (the features of milestones lp-calls-and-messages, lp-connected, lp-daily-basics; UBports' stages 3-4).

steps.title: Days without a reboot
steps.done_when: seven days of ordinary use with no reboot, crash or part lost
steps.guide: Reliability, not function (weiss-fosdem-2025-missing-20); UBports' noRebootTest (ubports-device-data).

steps.title: The display comes up at boot in any order
steps.done_when: on three cold boots the panel, its bridge and the GPU bind by deferred probe with their modules autoloaded (modalias), no initramfs module list or modprobe ordering of ours, and the console shows on the panel each time
steps.proof: display-boots-any-order: three boots; each boot's dmesg shows the panel bound after any deferral, lsmod lists the modules with no ordering file in the image, the panel lit
steps.guide: Upstream-readiness: a driver that only works with a hand-ordered module list is not ready for mainline. Return -EPROBE_DEFER for each supplier not yet there (regulators, the DSI host, the backlight, the GPIO expander), declare the suppliers in the device tree so fw_devlink orders it, and drop any modules-load or initramfs ordering list. walleye's B1 bring-up met the order dependence (walleye-display-s6e3fa5).

steps.title: dmesg clean
steps.done_when: no WARN, oops or -110, and no probe deferred but the known ones
steps.guide: walleye z7: the GPU smmu off cleared the gpu_gx WARNs (walleye-dmesg-clean); on a rootfs the suite's no-oops and boot-warnings carry it.

steps.title: The bootloader's dtbo overlay accepted
steps.done_when: our dtb, built with -@ and the overlay's labels, merges with the stock dtbo, or the bootloader does not need it
steps.guide: On walleye our dtb with -@ and the 137 labels merged; the dtbo stub that was planned was never needed (walleye-dtb-overlay-symbols-build, walleye-loaderror-dtbo-stub).

steps.title: The earpiece plays
steps.done_when: a tone through the earpiece is heard by the bottom microphone
steps.guide: surya: the earpiece is the second TAS256x at 0x4d, not the codec's EAR amplifier (parts row audio-earpiece).

steps.title: Emergency numbers are known
steps.done_when: the modem's emergency list is read, and 112 would be dialled as an emergency call even without a SIM - proven without dialling
steps.guide: Test to write. Android's rule: 112 and 911 always; the list from network, SIM, modem or defaults (android-emergency-call). surya open (volte-and-emergency).

steps.title: The DSP helpers run without crashing the DSP
steps.done_when: the FastRPC helpers (hexagonrpcd) serve and the DSP they talk to stays up over three boots
steps.guide: surya: the rootpd helper crashed the ADSP 24 times of 24 (2026-11-10-suspend-crash-found, adsp-sensor-crash-loop); masked in surya's device.toml.

steps.title: The fingerprint unlocks
steps.done_when: a finger enrols and unlocks through fprintd
steps.guide: surya: the reader is not exposed (reader-exposed fails, a declared gap). Most phone readers are not in libfprint.

steps.title: The device's firmware is reachable
steps.done_when: every firmware file the kernel asks for is found: no failed direct firmware load for a needed file
steps.guide: Signed blobs are the stock system's, per device: from the stock partitions read-only (msm-firmware-loader, which assumes eMMC) or a firmware package (pmos-firmware-docs; surya firmware-xiaomi-surya).

steps.title: The first dmesg mapped
steps.done_when: the first full dmesg of our kernel is read and every line placed: works, defers, fails, and whose
steps.guide: The map orders what follows (walleye-z6-dmesg-map, research walleye-bringup-order-plan).

steps.title: Focus and flash
steps.done_when: autofocus moves the lens to a sharp image and the flash fires
steps.guide: World gap: 3A tuning for phone sensors has no public prior art; focus-coil drivers were in review in 2025.

steps.title: The host sees our gadget
steps.done_when: the host enumerates our own kernel's gadget by its vendor:product and serial
steps.guide: walleye y2: 1d6b:0104 18 s after the jump (walleye-try-y).

steps.title: A position fix
steps.done_when: a fix outdoors within 5 minutes, reaching geoclue
steps.guide: On Qualcomm the location engine is the modem's (QMI LOC), through ModemManager and gnss-share. surya open (gps-measurable). World gap: no assisted GPS (XTRA) anywhere.

steps.title: The GPU renders
steps.done_when: a GL and a Vulkan client render on the GPU (not a software renderer) to the panel
steps.guide: Test to write; never measured in our labs. Adreno needs its zap shader and GMU firmware from the device.

steps.title: The vibrator buzzes
steps.done_when: a force-feedback effect is felt
steps.guide: The suite proves presence only; the buzz is a hand's witness. walleye open (walleye-audio-haptics, DRV2624).

steps.title: A headset works through the jack
steps.done_when: plugging is detected, sound plays to the headset and its microphone records
steps.guide: surya partial: detection only (verify-headphone-mic-earpiece). A loopback plug can prove both ways without hands.

steps.title: The health suite runs after every boot
steps.done_when: the phone's own suite runs after every boot and its run is filed in the device's base
steps.guide: From here a part's status is measured, not judged (surya 2026-11-17-health-on-the-phone).

steps.title: The phone shares its data
steps.done_when: a client on the phone's Wi-Fi hotspot reaches the internet over mobile data
steps.guide: Test to write; never tried.

steps.title: Each image sensor is identified
steps.done_when: each sensor's chip-id register reads its expected value in its slot
steps.guide: surya failing: the slots are being identified (camera-identify-slots).

steps.title: Our initramfs brings the gadget up, emulated
steps.done_when: in QEMU with dummy_hcd our initramfs makes the gadget (ACM console and a window) and the host side sees it
steps.guide: Prove the init before any phone time (walleye walleye-initramfs-usb-gadget). The generic init under lpoco is backlog bringup-generic-init.

steps.title: Our kernel and dts build
steps.done_when: the mainline kernel and the device's dts build with no dtc warning from our file, and the dtb carries the ids the bootloader matches
steps.guide: Start from the nearest sibling's dts in mainline (walleye from taimen, walleye-kernel-dts).

steps.title: Our kernel reaches our init
steps.done_when: our kernel and our dtb reach /init: the phone stays up as long as /init says, with no early reset
steps.guide: Two traps on walleye: earlycon on an undeclared UART kills the kernel (walleye-no-earlycon); a pinctrl node without gpio-reserved-ranges touches the secure world's pins and resets the phone (walleye-our-dts-gpio-reserved).

steps.title: A kernel upgrade keeps every step
steps.done_when: on a new kernel release the suite passes what it passed before, and proven_on moves to the new kernel
steps.guide: How claims stay true without expiry: a later kernel is told by proven_on and re-proven.

steps.title: A held key resets a hung phone
steps.done_when: holding power (with volume down where so wired) for the set time hard-resets a hung phone, and the next boot's reason says so
steps.guide: The PMIC's S1/S2 key reset, set by the firmware or the PON driver; a user's way back that needs no software. Test by hand.

steps.title: The lab's link holds the phone awake
steps.done_when: while a host holds the USB link, nothing suspends the phone, and the hold is released on purpose for sleep tests
steps.guide: surya: 26 link drops in 5 minutes before the hold (2026-11-10-usb-flapping), the screen blanking by itself (2026-11-18-screen-blanks-by-itself); held by devlab-usb-awake-hold-through-resume, moving to a package (surya-awake-from-package).

steps.title: Linux runs
steps.done_when: every step it needs is done or not-needed
steps.guide: A goal: it does nothing itself - done when every hard need is done or not-needed, read off tad q bringup-chain (its ready is its done). A group of groups, as a systemd target is (systemd-target). The close of the generic bring-up, any machine.

steps.title: Lock and unlock
steps.done_when: the power key locks and darkens; the phone unlocks with its code
steps.guide: Needs the keys clean of chatter (buttons-report).

steps.title: The microphones capture
steps.done_when: a second of capture from each microphone is not digital silence
steps.guide: surya: zeros meant the link named the wrong DAI (mic-zeros-meant-no-input); the mics are analog through the WCD, ADC2 on its own port (2026-11-17-microphones-analog-wcd-path).

steps.title: Each microphone hears the speaker
steps.done_when: each microphone finds the phone's own tone 20 dB above the noise
steps.guide: A closed loop with no hands: surya done (mic-held).

steps.title: MMS both ways
steps.done_when: a picture message sent to the phone's own number comes back
steps.guide: Test to write; never tried in our labs (mmsd-tng).

steps.title: Mobile data
steps.done_when: pings and a 100 kB download go over the bearer's own interface, so Wi-Fi cannot stand in
steps.guide: surya: naming the APN gave 'Multiple PDN connection', so the connection carries none (modem-online-tqftpserv); budget mobile-data-check-budget.

steps.title: The modem's file services serve
steps.done_when: rmtfs, the qrtr name service, pd-mapper and tqftpserv run and the modem's mode is online, not shutting down
steps.guide: surya: tqftpserv 1.1.1 never wrote short files and the modem looped 4769 times; 1.2 or later fixed it (modem-online-tqftpserv, upstream-alpine-tqftpserv).

steps.title: The modem joins the network
steps.done_when: the modem is registered on a network
steps.guide: Read-only first (2026-11-11-modem-read-only-first). surya done.

steps.title: The modem is seen
steps.done_when: ModemManager (or oFono) lists the modem
steps.guide: On Qualcomm SoCs through the qcom-soc plugin over QRTR and IPA or BAM-DMUX (mm-qcom-soc-plugin).

steps.title: NFC reads a tag
steps.done_when: a tag held to the phone is read
steps.guide: surya: the controller probes (nfc-device), nothing reads tags. World gap: NFC unclaimed on these phones.

steps.title: Notifications arrive with the screen off
steps.done_when: a message or a call shows a notification and sounds while the screen is off
steps.guide: Push for apps is a service (feature push-notifications), not a step.

steps.title: Charges while off
steps.done_when: plugged in while off it charges, shows its level, and boots on the power key
steps.guide: Sailfish names it act-dead mode (sailfish-hadk-checklist). World gap: the usual tool, charging-sdl, is unmaintained and boot-loops at low battery (pmaports-charging-sdl-1064).

steps.title: The on-screen keyboard types
steps.done_when: the keyboard comes up in a text field and types into it
steps.guide: Witness for now; a robot finger or an input injection can stand in.

steps.title: The panel lights
steps.done_when: the console or a test pattern shows on the panel and the backlight follows its control
steps.guide: Qualcomm DSI panels: a driver generated from the downstream tree (lmdpdg). walleye needs a command-mode panel driver (walleye-display-s6e3fa5).

steps.title: The domain mapper is up before the DSPs
steps.done_when: the protection-domain mapper serves before qcom_q6v5_pas probes, so the audio domain comes up on 20 boots of 20
steps.guide: surya: 8 boots of 42 had no sound card without a softdep (no-sound-card-boots; surya-lab lab/devlab-pd-mapper.conf), 21 of 21 with it; the upstream form is open (upstream-pd-mapper-order). The mapper is in the kernel since 2024 (inkernel-pd-mapper).

steps.title: A photo
steps.done_when: a capture tool saves a photo with sane exposure and colour from each camera
steps.guide: Fairphone 6: all three cameras in 2026, the furthest any Qualcomm phone got (linmob-weekly-34-2026). Proven in the test layer with a capture tool; a shell's camera app is the shell's own use of it (2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer).

steps.title: The PMIC bound
steps.done_when: the PMIC's children bind on their bus, the RTC and the power-on reason read
steps.guide: walleye: pm8998 and pmi8998 on SPMI (walleye-pmic-spmi, proven in z7). UFS rails are RPM regulators and do not wait for it (walleye-bringup-order-plan).

steps.title: Why it turned on, and why it last turned off, are read
steps.done_when: each boot logs the power-on reason (key, USB charger, RTC alarm, warm reset, watchdog, key-combo reset) and the last power-off reason, read from the PMIC
steps.guide: Test to write. On Qualcomm the PON block keeps PON_REASON, WARM_RESET_REASON and POFF_REASON (gen2 moves POFF_REASON1 to 0xc5; downstream-qpnp-power-on-sm6150 logs them, mainline's qcom-pon does not show them). surya read its PON registers by hand (surya-lab PR 269; upstreams-lane). Every step of the off side is told apart by this reason.

steps.title: Off stays off
steps.done_when: poweroff leaves the machine off, and plugging a charger in does not boot the full system
steps.guide: surya fails: poweroff and a plugged charger both boot pmOS (off-state-charging); only the old eOS recovery's power-off held, so the PMIC can stay off and our power-off path is what differs. Read the power-on reason (pon-reason-read) and the reset types (reset-types-right) to tell a reboot from a charger power-on.

steps.title: The screen goes dark at the ear
steps.done_when: in a call the screen blanks and touch is ignored while the proximity sensor is covered
steps.guide: surya open (sensors-proximity-in-calls). Sailfish checks it while suspended too (sailfish-hadk-checklist).

steps.title: Proximity reads near and far
steps.done_when: covering the sensor changes its reading from far to near and back
steps.guide: surya partial: covering it waits a witness (sensors-proximity-cover-witnessed).

steps.title: The radios come back from sleep
steps.done_when: after 20 cycles Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are up, with no interrupt storm and no controller crash
steps.guide: surya partial: the CTS pull-down hung the boot (2026-11-18-cts-pulldown-dtb-hangs); serial wakeup off (2026-11-17-serial-wakeup-off, 2026-11-18-bt-suspend-way).

steps.title: A raw frame
steps.done_when: one raw frame from each sensor arrives through the receiver
steps.guide: Test to write. Sensor drivers are often out of tree (Pixel 3a, OnePlus 6).

steps.title: The shell's own suspend returns
steps.done_when: the shell's auto-suspend and systemctl suspend return, again and again
steps.guide: surya failing: the phone did not return (2026-11-18-real-suspend-try4-phone-did-not-return). The hardware's suspend steps (s2idle-cycle-returns, radios-survive-suspend, suspend-way-back) are proven first in the test layer; this one is the shell's own idle suspend and systemctl suspend, per shell (2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer).

steps.title: Someone else's mainline kernel boots here
steps.done_when: another project's mainline kernel and dtb for this device or a sibling reach their init on this phone
steps.guide: The reference to bisect against when ours is dead: swap one part at a time (walleye pk5 alive against ours dead: walleye-bisect-porthole-vs-ours, walleye-our-dtb-bisect, walleye-property-bisect).

steps.title: Every coprocessor runs
steps.done_when: every remoteproc the device has reads running and none crashed this boot
steps.guide: surya done; walleye open (walleye-radios-research). Trap: the ADSP 'handover signaled' every second (adsp-handover-loop).

steps.title: What must survive a reset does, and the rest is set again
steps.done_when: across a warm reset the reboot mode (the PMIC's spare register: bootloader, recovery), the RTC and ramoops survive; after any reset the kernel sets again the PMIC state it relies on (S2 reset type, watchdogs) and reads it back
steps.guide: The PMIC keeps its registers across a warm reset and the firmware rewrites some at boot (surya's S2 type 0x01 from firmware, upstreams-lane). ramoops survives a warm reset only if its memory is not cleared (ramoops-doc). Test to write.

steps.title: Power-off, reboot and a bite each reach the right PMIC reset
steps.done_when: power-off ends in the PMIC's shutdown, reboot in a warm or hard reset, and a watchdog bite in a hard reset - each read back from the PMIC and seen in the next boot's reason
steps.guide: On Qualcomm, power-off goes by PSCI SYSTEM_OFF to the secure firmware, which sets the PS_HOLD reset type and drops PS_HOLD; reboot sets another type. A wrong type, the firmware's own choice, or a power-on trigger still pending (a plugged cable, an armed PMIC watchdog, an RTC alarm) turns off into a new boot. surya: the firmware leaves S2 at warm reset 0x01; patch 5/5 sets hard reset 0x07 with a read-back (upstreams-lane). walleye: a bite powered off instead of restarting (pmic-wdt-reset-type). Test to write.

steps.title: Resume without a stall
steps.done_when: 20 attended cycles with no coprocessor crash and no RCU stall
steps.guide: surya failing (2026-11-18-resume-stall-how-it-stands, resume-stall-stop-clients).

steps.title: A distribution root boots
steps.done_when: a distribution's root filesystem boots to its init and ssh answers
steps.guide: surya boots Nura through U-Boot, systemd-boot and an EFI kernel (first-fastboot-probe).

steps.title: An alarm turns the phone on from off
steps.done_when: an alarm set before power-off turns the phone on at its time, and the reason reads RTC alarm
steps.guide: Android's power-off alarm: the PMIC RTC alarm powers it up and the bootloader boots an alarm mode. PCs have rtcwake -m off. World gap: no mainline phone distribution sets an alarm that survives power-off, and whether rtc-pm8xxx keeps the alarm armed through shutdown is not known yet.

steps.title: A timed suspend returns
steps.done_when: a 15 s RTC-timed suspend returns in the same boot
steps.guide: surya partial (health-suspend-cycle-proof): woke at once (2026-11-17-surya-s2idle-wakes-at-once), a UART wake across suspend (2026-11-17-qca-uart-wake-across-suspend). These SoCs have s2idle only (qcom-sleep-path).

steps.title: The sensor hub runs without crashing its DSP
steps.done_when: the sensor domain runs with no DSP crash over three boots
steps.guide: surya: the registry kept current and a hexagonrpcd patch (2026-11-17-sensors-registry-kept-current, 2026-11-17-sensors-lasting-install-three-boots). World gap: why registry writes fail on some firmware.

steps.title: Sensors come back from sleep
steps.done_when: the sensor helper is stopped before suspend and serves again after
steps.guide: FastRPC helpers attached across suspend crash the ADSP: surya and the Pixel 3a stop them around it (2026-11-18-systemctl-suspend-leaves-sensors-stopped, sleep-fastrpc-helpers).

steps.title: Motion and light sensors read
steps.done_when: accelerometer, gyroscope and light give changing values through iio-sensor-proxy
steps.guide: surya done (motion-and-light; the test once counted devices only, sensors-hardware-surya). Behind the Qualcomm DSP through libssc (iio-sensor-proxy-libssc).

steps.title: The shell's idle suspend is held off while the lab works
steps.done_when: the shell's own idle suspend is off or held off while the lab works, proven per shell (sxmo's autosleep, Phosh's gsd-power, Plasma Mobile's PowerDevil)
steps.guide: surya: sxmo's rtcwake loop cut the lab off (2026-11-18-who-runs-rtcwake-99999999). The test layer has no shell to hold off, so the hardware steps do not wait on this; it is the shell's own, once for each shell, and the sxmo fork and its series are retired (2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer).

steps.title: A shell answers on the console
steps.done_when: commands sent on the console answer, one at a time, reliably across hangups
steps.guide: On walleye an interactive ash stayed silent; a plain read/exec loop and the host tty raw and -hupcl made it answer (walleye-shell-reliable, walleye-command-loop, walleye-try-z6).

steps.title: A phone shell runs on the hardware
steps.done_when: a phone shell (sxmo, Phosh, Plasma Mobile) starts on the panel with touch, sound to the real card and its device profile
steps.guide: surya: sxmo with its profile; under Phosh the host loses the USB link (phosh-usb); Plasma was silent from a saved -110 dB mixer (plasma-silent). Phosh and Plasma need the GPU, sxmo does not.

steps.title: The SIM is read
steps.done_when: the SIM reads present and unlocked, in each slot the device has
steps.guide: surya: the SIM works only in slot 2 (modem-online-tqftpserv); checks that need a SIM skip, not fail, without one (sim-removed-skips).

steps.title: Slots read, a way back known
steps.done_when: both slots' flags are reported before and after every try, and the phone returns to the stock system by itself
steps.guide: On walleye the Load Error was the slot state left by refusals, not the image: restore the first state (Android booted to completion on a good slot) before each try (walleye-load-error-first-state).

steps.title: SMS both ways
steps.done_when: a message sent to the phone's own number comes back
steps.guide: surya done (tests/health/telephony/sms-loopback.sh); it costs money, so it runs at most once a day.

steps.title: The SoC reaches its floor
steps.done_when: in suspend the SoC's deepest-state counters rise (on Qualcomm: CX collapse and AOSS sleep)
steps.guide: surya failing: cxsd, aosd and ddr stay 0 (2026-11-17-adsp-stopped-cx-aosd-ddr-stay-0, sleep-cluster-params). World gap: no public example of that floor on an SM7150/845-class phone (2026-11-17-floor-research).

steps.title: The sound card registers
steps.done_when: the machine's card is listed on every boot
steps.guide: surya: lost on 8 boots of 42 until the domain mapper was ordered (no-sound-card-boots).

steps.title: The amplifiers get their channels
steps.done_when: each speaker amplifier gets its slot and is unmuted at the chip, not only in the driver's cache
steps.guide: surya tas2562: the slot length (upstream-tas2562-slot-length) and a volume write that reached only the cache (plasma-silent, upstream-tas2562-volume).

steps.title: The speaker is heard
steps.done_when: a quiet tone on each channel is heard by the lab's ear
steps.guide: Quiet tones only. surya: one 'heard' was withdrawn when the microphone had moved (2026-11-10-heard).

steps.title: Standby draws little
steps.done_when: on battery alone, asleep with the modem attached, the average current is under the device's target (15 mA on surya)
steps.guide: The arbiter of sleep (2026-11-17-standby-current-is-the-arbiter). surya partial: median 31 mA (2026-11-17-r3-partial-and-the-reset-after). World gap: no published s2idle figures per SoC with a modem. Measured first in the test layer, with no shell to wake it; the shell's figure follows under real-suspend-under-shell (2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer).

steps.title: The stock boot's facts read
steps.done_when: the stock cmdline, boot header and offsets, dtb ids (msm-id, board-id), running fdt and ramoops region are recorded
steps.guide: Read them from the running stock system and its boot image (walleye walleye-stock-ids-recorded, walleye-boot-cmdline-known). The running fdt is worth keeping whole: on walleye it named the cause of the dead dtbs (walleye-our-dts-gpio-reserved).

steps.title: The stock kernel runs our init
steps.done_when: the stock kernel with only our ramdisk swapped runs our /init, and it shows (a gadget, a mass-storage window)
steps.guide: Proves the image path apart from our kernel. On walleye the NCM function panics the vendor 4.4 kernel; a mass-storage window works (walleye-ncm-split, walleye-massstorage-window).

steps.title: The stock system measured
steps.done_when: what works on the stock system, its battery and its partitions are recorded as the reference
steps.guide: Measure the stock system before anything is flashed: it is the reference 'as good as Android' is judged by, and an unlock may wipe it (walleye android-reference-walleye-measured).

steps.title: Internal storage links at full speed
steps.done_when: the internal storage's link runs at the fastest mode the SoC and the card both support - UFS: the HS gear and lane count of the SoC's spec, both lanes up; eMMC: HS400 (or HS200 where HS400 is not supported) - read from the kernel, and a sequential read measures within reach of that mode
steps.proof: storage-link-speed: the link mode from debugfs or dmesg (UFS power mode HS-Gn, lanes; eMMC timing) matches the SoC's documented maximum, and a read-only dd of a partition measures the throughput
steps.guide: Upstream-readiness: a storage driver that links at PWM or one lane boots but is not done. On Qualcomm UFS the PHY tables and the gear limits per SoC decide it; compare with the downstream tree's settings. Read only: never write the internal storage to measure it.

steps.title: Internal storage read-only
steps.done_when: the internal storage lists its partitions by name, nothing written
steps.guide: Gives the firmware partitions every later part needs (walleye-ufs-readonly).

steps.title: Only the meant sources wake it
steps.done_when: over a suspend only the RTC, the modem, the keys and the charger wake it
steps.guide: surya partial (floor-irq-quiet); ath10k floods the modem's interrupt on sdm845 (qcom-sleep-blockers).

steps.title: A hang in sleep finds its way back
steps.done_when: a hang in or after suspend resets the machine or panics into ramoops
steps.guide: Extends watchdog-way-back into sleep. surya: the stock watchdog stops in suspend (2026-11-17-surya-way-back-inventory), kept armed by a patch (qcom-wdt-keep-armed-in-suspend); walleye: the PMIC watchdog bit and did not return (walleye-pmic-bite-reset-type-how-it-stands).

steps.title: The test layer boots, with no shell
steps.done_when: a boot with no phone shell (multi-user.target, no display manager) is up with a tty, ssh and the lab's services, and nothing in it suspends, locks or reacts to keys unless a test asks; the lab's suspend work runs there
steps.guide: Hardware steps are proven here, the shell's own in the shell stage (2026-11-19-hardware-test-layer). lab-tools' health-test-layer-quiet reads it: no shell or idle-suspend process runs, logind's IdleAction and HandlePowerKey are ignore, no suspend this boot but the health suite's own cycles; in a shell layer it says skip and names the shell, so the step stays unknown until the test layer boots. surya: the image it runs, booted from a second entry with systemd.unit=multi-user.target, the sxmo entry beside it. A new device's first root filesystem is this layer. Measured: test-layer-sxmo-cost-measured, test-layer-landscape.

steps.title: Thermal zones read and throttle
steps.done_when: every thermal zone reads a plausible temperature, trips are set, and a load throttles before any shutdown
steps.guide: Test to write; never touched in our labs. Android has a thermal HAL and a policy; Linux phones have the kernel's zones and no policy daemon (aosp-compat-matrix, sailfish-hadk-checklist).

steps.title: Touch answers
steps.done_when: a touch at each corner gives events at the right coordinates
steps.guide: surya done; walleye open (walleye-touch-rmi4). The suite proves presence; coordinates need a hand or a robot.

steps.title: Kernel log on UART
steps.done_when: the kernel's log reaches the host over the debug UART
steps.guide: Needs the device's debug cable or pads; on walleye it waits the cable (walleye-get-uart-setup), so the USB gadget was the console.

steps.title: A UCM profile plays to the real card
steps.done_when: the shell's sound server picks the card's HiFi verb and plays in stereo, the right channel to the right speaker
steps.guide: surya ucm/Xiaomi/surya/HiFi.conf (2026-11-11-right-is-bottom), upstream open (upstream-ucm-surya-stereo).

steps.title: An update applies
steps.done_when: an update from the distribution applies over the air and the phone boots it, the health suite as before
steps.guide: Test to write. UBports proves it by a local OTA test before an installer (ubports-porting).

steps.title: A bad update rolls back
steps.done_when: an update that does not boot falls back to the last good one with no hands
steps.guide: A/B slots (qbootctl) or a boot counter; Android's boot control HAL (aosp-compat-matrix).

steps.title: USB host works
steps.done_when: the port switches to host and a plugged device enumerates
steps.guide: Switching the port cuts the lab's USB link: a second way in first.

steps.title: Network over USB
steps.done_when: ssh over the USB gadget's network answers
steps.guide: walleye: walleye-usb-net. surya had the distribution's own gadget.

steps.title: A video with sound
steps.done_when: a recorded video plays back with its sound in step
steps.guide: Never tried in our labs.

steps.title: A call carries sound both ways
steps.done_when: a tone sent into a call comes back from an echo line
steps.guide: Proven by an echo call, no hands (2026-11-17-calls-proven-by-echo-call, echo-call-test-design). surya done.

steps.title: A call over LTE
steps.done_when: a call is known to go over IMS and carries sound both ways
steps.guide: World gap: no open IMS works across carriers; 81voltd serves the IMS data service on some phones and carriers, OpenIMSd reverse-engineers the rest, one emergency VoLTE call on a Fairphone 6 (linmob-weekly-34-2026). surya open (volte-and-emergency).

steps.title: A hung kernel comes back by itself
steps.done_when: a hung kernel resets by itself and the phone returns to a known system without hands
steps.guide: surya: qcom_wdt kept armed through sleep (way-back.sh). walleye: the PMIC watchdog (walleye-pmic-wdt-proof).

steps.title: Wi-Fi joins and reaches the gateway
steps.done_when: the interface joins a network and reaches its gateway
steps.guide: walleye open: the WCN3990 firmware from the vendor partition (walleye-wifi-wcn3990). 5 GHz and speed never measured.
